To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep convolutional networks are kernel machines with a hierarchical kernel, and that their RKHS consists of functions that can be decomposed into additive terms of interactions between patches.

1. The RKHS of a hierarchical kernel inspired by convolutional networks consists of additive functions over patches, 2. The RKHS norm encourages similarity of interaction terms through the pooling layers, and 3. The sample complexity of the RKHS is improved when the target function has such regularities

(1) convolutional kernel networks can approximate functions that are additive models of interaction between patches, (2) convolutional kernel network RKHSs can encourage such additive models to have similar interaction terms, and (3) this inductive bias can improve generalization bounds for functions that have this form
In summary, our research is concerned with
a precise understanding of the function class induced by deep convolutional networks.
the following question: what is the function class that a deep convolutional model can approximate efficiently?
the study of convolutional networks as kernel methods, which allows for a precise characterization of their inductive bias in terms of the RKHS they induce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the convolutional neural network is a powerful model that is well-suited to the task of image classification, and that it is able to achieve this because it has an inductive bias towards functions that can be well-approximated by convolutional kernels, which is exactly the type of function that is well-suved to the task of classifying images.

the convolutional kernel network architecture provides an effective way of approximating functions which are additive over small patches, with the added benefit of encouraging the spatial similarity of these patches.
convolution and pooling in the RKHS are good inductive biases for learning functions that can be well approximated by a combination of patches, and which have spatially coherent dependencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a kernel-theoretic perspective on the inductive bias of deep convolutional models, and that this perspective allows us to better understand and analyze the benefits of convolutional architectures.
we study the approximation and generalization properties of deep convolutional models from the perspective of kernel methods.
deep learning is kernel learning with a twist.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inductive bias of deep convolutional architectures, which has been largely studied from a geometric perspective, is also well-motivated from a functional perspective.

the success of convolutional models is not only due to their ability to capture local interactions in the data (as is often argued), but also to their ability to learn global interactions between these local features.
the inductive bias of convolutional models is well-motivated by the structure of the target functions, and that this bias is captured by a kernel-based perspective.
